title: iQSTEL: attacker at GlobeTopper redeemed gift cards worth approximately $70,000 and took business customers' API keys
date_note: Disclosure: iQSTEL's SEC 8-K (Item 8.01) is signed 20 November 2026. It says GlobeTopper identified the unauthorized access on 22 October 2026, more than seven days earlier.
geo_basis: parent company iQSTEL's principal executive offices on the SEC filing's cover page; GlobeTopper's own location is not stated
summary: iQSTEL told the SEC that its subsidiary GlobeTopper identified unauthorized access to its platform on 22 October, took it offline on 23 October, and resumed operations in stages from 1 November. According to the filing, digital gift cards with a face value of approximately $70,000 were redeemed and the attacker obtained some business customers' API credentials and integration keys, since revoked and rotated. BleepingComputer reports an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue.
plain: A gift card company owned by iQSTEL says hackers got into its platform in October, redeemed gift cards worth approximately $70,000 and took some business customers' API keys, which were then replaced.
exec: A B2B gift card platform says an attacker took business customers' API credentials and redeemed approximately $70,000 in gift cards; lost revenue is put at an estimated $2.5 million.
action: No action needed; for awareness. iQSTEL says all affected credentials and integration keys have been revoked and rotated and affected business customers were issued new ones.

sources.name: iQSTEL Inc. Form 8-K (SEC), report dated 16 November 2026
BleepingComputer: GlobeTopper loses $2.5 million after hackers steal $70k in gift cards

evidence.quote: digital gift cards with an aggregate face value of approximately $70,000 were redeemed without authorization
A cyberattack disrupted operations at B2B top-up solutions provider GlobeTopper, causing an estimated $2.5 million in lost revenue, while the attacker redeemed digital gift cards worth $70,000.

validation.note: Primary source: iQSTEL's own SEC 8-K, read in full; BleepingComputer reports the same filing. The filing calls the $2.5 million management's preliminary high-end estimate of revenue not generated and says the incident has not been determined to be material.

review.note: Compared title, dates, 70,000 USD face value, API keys rotated, 2.5M estimate and materiality statement against SEC 8-K and BleepingComputer
